finding.why: web:Ezek.2.1 run “He said to me, ‘Son of man, stand on your feet’” is accurate as far as it goes but stops before the witness does, and the spliced Hebrew it glosses runs on through wa-adabber otak (“and I will speak with you”). Gloss extent != splice extent (E-08 in §8).
‘one of five’ carries a digit but no swept OBJECT or UNIT, which §8 requires; as written it is ambiguous between two defensible sweeps and wrong under the Hebrew one.
'(sweep: 1 verse)' names a digit but not the swept OBJECT or UNIT, so the absence claim it is meant to source is unsourced as written (§8 requires the object named first, then the count).

observations: NEAR/FAR WORDING IN PROSE runs against the ruled rival convention (near = candidate onset verse) in three rows no item opens for prose: P01-009 SRA calls 5:4 the rival's near face and 5:5 its far face; P02-003 SRA calls 8:15 the near face and 8:16 the far face; P03-007 SRA calls 16:51 the far face (true of the row's own close seam, not of the rival). The tokens follow the ruling; the prose is left for the prose pass.

Several SRAs still use near/far in the older before/after sense for rivals (P01-009 5:4/5:5, P02-003 8:15/8:16); where the old refs gloss said 'far face' on a candidate-onset verse it was re-glossed (S4-006, S4-020, S4-059) so no entry contradicts its qualifier. The prose itself is not in any item's order and is left for the prose pass (the brief's worklist notes P11-001 and P11-013 are already there).
data.rule: clause 6 v2: for a rival, near is the candidate onset verse and far the verse behind it
